verses.1: And one of the women among the daughters of the prophets cried out to Elijah, saying, “My servant has died. You know that your servant feared Jehovah. The murderer came to take both his sons as slaves.”
verses.2: And Elisha said to her, “What shall I do? Tell me, what will you have in the house?” She replied, “There is nothing in your house except for some wood.”
verses.3: And he said to him, “I ask you to take away all the offerings from your neighbors. Take away only the clean offerings; do not touch the rest.”
verses.4: And you shall come and close the door, along with your children. You shall also pour water over all these utensils. Then the filling will be ready.
verses.5: She went away from him, and she closed the door behind her and her children. They tried to get inside, but she refused to let them in.
verses.6: And when all the dishes were filled, she said to her daughter, “Bring them to me again.” But her daughter said, “There’s nothing left for me.” And the pot stood there.
verses.7: And she went and reported to the man of God. He said to her, “I will take you as my wife, and I will bless you and your children. You shall live in peace.”
verses.8: And it came to pass that on that day, Elisha went to Shunem. There, there was a very rich woman who provided him with food to eat. As he continued to travel, he felt hungry and needed to find something to eat.
verses.9: And she said to her husband, “Please know that there is a man who is holy and divine. He always remains above us.”
verses.10: Please make a small wall above me, and put there a table, a chair, a bed, and a lamp. This will serve as a place where we can come to meet with each other.
verses.11: And it came to pass that the day came, and Shammah went up to the hill, and he lay down there.
verses.12: And he said to his young man, “Call out to that woman.” So he called out to her, and she stood before him.
verses.13: And he said to her, “Please, tell her that she should be afraid. She has brought all this fear upon us. What should she do? She should speak with the king or with the chief priests.” But she replied, “In my people’s midst, I will sit.”
verses.14: And he said, “What should I do with her?” He replied, “Give her a son. But she has no son; instead, she has an old man.”
verses.15: And he said, “Call her.” So he called out to her. And she stood at the door.
verses.16: And he said to the priest, “At this time, you are still alive. You are still a son of God. So say, ‘O Lord, do not abandon your people.’”
verses.17: And the woman arose and gave birth to a son on that day. He was alive, as Elijah had said to her.
verses.18: And the child grew up. One day, he went to see his father at the market.
verses.19: And he said to his father, “Roshi! Roshi!” And he also said to the boy who carried him to his mother.
verses.20: And he carried him away and brought him to his mother. He sat on her lap until dawn came, and then he died.
verses.21: And she laid him on the lap of a man of God, and she covered him with a blanket. Then she left.
verses.22: And she called out to one of her women servants and said, “Send me one of the boys and one of the maidens. Let them go to the house of the God, and then return.”
verses.23: And Mada said, “You are going to him today, not on the New Year, nor on Shabbat. Then Shalom said…”
verses.24: And she touched her hair and said to the girl, “Go ahead and walk away from me. Do not stop until I say so.”
verses.25: And she went and arrived at the man of God, at Mount Carmel. Then the man of God looked at her from afar and said to his servant, “Look! This woman is a prostitute.”
verses.26: Now, please read it aloud. And say to her: “May peace be upon you, upon your husband, and upon the child.” Then she will say, “Peace.”
verses.27: And she went to the God’s man, to the mountain. She strengthened her legs and rushed towards him. The God’s man said, “Relax her, for she is already weak.” But Jehovah did not tell me anything about this.
verses.28: And she said, “I have asked you, son of my master. But you did not say, ‘Do not give me this.’”
verses.29: And he said to Gideon, “Tie up your sandals and take my staff with you. Go ahead, and if you find anyone who doesn’t bless you, don’t bless them either. And if someone does bless you, don’t refuse their blessing either. Then place my staff on the face of the boy.”
verses.30: And the mother said, “May the boy live, may Jehovah and your soul be blessed. If I leave you, then he will rise up and go after her.”
verses.31: And Gachzi passed by them. He placed the bandage on the boy’s face. There was no sound, and no response from the boy. Then he sat down again and began to call out to him, saying, “The boy hasn’t woken up yet.”
verses.32: And Elisha entered the house. There, he saw that the boy was dead, lying on his bed.
verses.33: And he came and closed the door, for both of them. Then he prayed to Jehovah.
verses.34: And he lay down on the child, with his mouth over the child’s mouth, and his eyes over the child’s eyes, and his head over the child’s head. Then he became angry with the child, and his breath became hot on the child’s body.
verses.35: And he sat down and walked around the house from one side to the other. Then he got up and became angry with him. He yelled at the boy seven times. Finally, the boy opened his eyes.
verses.36: And he called out to Giehazi, and said, “Call out to that Shunamit.” She did as she was told. She came to him, and he said, “Lay down your son.”
verses.37: And she came in, and she knelt on her knees. She bowed down to the ground, and she carried her child in her arms. Then she left.
verses.38: Elisha returned from the wilderness. Famine had come upon the land. The prophets sat before him. He said to his young man, “Speak loudly and shout for the prophets to hear.”
verses.39: And one of them went into the field to gather fruits. He found a vineyard full of ripe grapes. He picked some of the grapes and brought them back with him. But they didn’t know what to do with those grapes.
verses.40: They offered food to the people to eat. But as they ate from that food, they became sick. They cried out in pain, saying, “Death has come upon us!” They couldn’t eat any more.
verses.41: And he said, “Take some bread and throw it into the pot. Then say to the people, ‘Eat it.’ There was no harm in the pot at all.”
verses.42: And a man came from the owner of three flocks. He brought to the Lord of God forty pieces of bread, along with some fruit and honey in his basket. He said, “Give this to the people so that they can eat it.”
verses.43: And his servant said, “What shall I give this before a hundred men?” He replied, “Give it to the people, so that they may eat it. For as Jehovah has said, ‘Eat and be satisfied.’”
verses.44: And he gave them food to eat, and they ate according to Jehovah’s command.
